definition: Major depressive disorder is a condition marked by a noticeable change in how a person is functioning, with at least two weeks of symptoms that include depressed mood or loss of interest or pleasure. It also involves several other possible symptoms, such as changes in sleep or weight, low energy, slowed or agitated movement, guilt or worthlessness, trouble thinking or deciding, or thoughts of death or suicide.

provenance.scope: Source record D003865; pinned source text

reasons: The definition omits a key criterion in the packet: the disorder requires five or more symptoms during the same 2-week period, not just a 2-week period with some listed symptoms.

The symptom list is only partly supported as written because the packet specifies additional qualifying frequency/threshold wording (for example, nearly every day for several symptoms), which the definition leaves out.

The packet states that the disorder requires “five (or more) of the following symptoms” during the same 2-week period, but the definition does not include this requirement (it only requires at least two weeks with depressed mood or loss of interest/pleasure).

The packet’s symptom descriptions include frequency qualifiers (e.g., “most of the day, nearly every day”), whereas the definition summarizes symptoms more generally without matching those qualifiers—making it less defensible relative to the packet.
